$meta.description: A `shell` object can be acquired by either using [get_shell](#GENERAL_GET_SHELL), [connect_service](#SHELL_CONNECT_SERVICE) or [overflow](#METALIB_OVERFLOW). The `classID` used for this object is `"shell"`. In case you want to use [connect_service](#SHELL_CONNECT_SERVICE) to connect to a SSH port it will be usually at port `22`.

start_terminal.description: Starts a terminal on the shell's computer in place of the running script, as the shell's user and in their home folder. It runs the computer's `/bin/bash` when that is a compiled script, otherwise the game's default bash. The terminal's color changes, displaying the IP of the connected shell. The script pauses until the terminal is closed with `exit`, then continues with an empty custom object and returns `1`; a script started with `shell.launch` loses its process. From then on, network functions such as `get_router` also need the shell's computer to be running. Returns null when not called on a shell, and `Unknown error: Unable to access to local computer` when the shell's computer no longer exists. Using this method within an SSH encryption process throws an error, preventing further script execution.

build.description: Builds source into a binary and returns an empty `string` on success or an error `string` on failure. Invalid argument types return `"build: Invalid arguments"`; source and destination paths require execute permission on every parent folder.
example: print("There was an error while compiling: " + buildResult)

connect_service.description: Connects to SSH or FTP and returns a shell, or an error `string` on failure. Invalid arguments and missing internet now return strings. Valid credentials for a dead or fired NPC return `"This account is disabled."`; SSH encryption still raises.
example: print("There was an error while connecting: " + connectionResult)

launch.description: Launches a binary synchronously and returns one once it starts, zero or an error `string` when it cannot start. Invalid argument types return `"launch: Invalid arguments"`. On a remote shell the program starts in that user's home folder. Execute permission is required on every parent folder; SSH encryption still raises.

ping.description: Returns one for a reachable address, zero for an unreachable one, and an error `string` for invalid input. Signature mismatches return `"ping: Invalid arguments"` instead of raising.

scp.description: Copies files between shells and returns one on complete success. Invalid arguments return `"scp: Invalid arguments"`. If nested items are skipped, returns `"Warning: one or more files or folders cannot be copied."`; SSH encryption still raises.
example: print("There was an error while sending file: " + result)
